And the concession that costs this lesson most: it has replaced a wrong number with a correct method and made the method sound easier than it is. Counting q and p on your own instrument means defining an approach, a level, a run and a reclaim in advance, then not adjusting them when the answer comes out uncomfortable. Every quoted frequency in this field was produced by somebody who adjusted them. The arithmetic on this page is the easy part, and the discipline it requires is the part that fails. Lesson 62 is where that discipline gets written down as a sentence, and it opens by judging one ordinary observation twice: 6 of 9 beats a coin and is adopted, and the same 6 of 9 against a 54.24 per cent baseline settles nothing at all.
